title: Your first check: expected vs observed
summary: Drake's first habit for anyone building with agents: write the expected answer before you look, compare it exactly with what you observe, and prove your check can fail. In this lesson two word counters both say 2 on 'hello world'; a real check on four tricky inputs catches three wrong answers in one of them, while a weak 'did it run?' check passes both. I can run it for you.
goal: Write a check that compares expected with observed, and make sure it can actually fail.
key_steps: Write the expected answer before running anything
Choose inputs that could trip the program up, not only the easy one
Keep one known-wrong version as a negative control
Distrust any check that has never failed

example.code:
note wc2: how many words are in the input? (second try)
text KW "\n"
note helpers: read all of stdin into inb, walk lines, compare a line prefix with the n-th
note entry of the newline separated table KW, and write table entries, input bytes and numbers
global inb uchar 65536
global num uchar 24
fn rdall to long
t = ulong 0
while lt t len inb bound 65536
k = read 0 inb t sub len inb t
if lt k 0
ret k
end
if eq k 0
ret long t
end
t = add t ulong k
end
ret neg long 27
end
fn eol s ulong n ulong to ulong
i = s
while lt i n bound 65536
if eq get inb i 10
ret i
end
i = add i 1
end
ret n
end
fn kstart k ulong to ulong
p = ulong 0
c = ulong 0
while lt c k bound 4096
if eq get KW p 10
c = add c 1
end
p = add p 1
end
ret p
end
fn klen k ulong to ulong
s = kstart k
i = s
while ne get KW i 10 bound 4096
i = add i 1
end
ret sub i s
end
fn pmat at ulong e ulong k ulong to bool
o = kstart k
m = klen k
if gt m sub e at
ret false
end
for j ulong m
if ne get inb add at j get KW add o j
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
fn emitk o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 4096
w = write 1 KW add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emiti o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 65536
w = write 1 inb add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn emitn o ulong n ulong to void
d = ulong 0
while lt d n bound 24
w = write 1 num add o d sub n d
if le w 0
trap 9
end
d = add d ulong w
end
end
fn say k ulong to void
emitk kstart k add klen k 1
end
fn word k ulong to void
emitk kstart k klen k
end
fn emitu v ulong to void
p = ulong 24
x = v
while true bound 21
p = sub p 1
put num p uchar add rem x 10 48
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
emitn p sub 24 p
end
note second try: count the places where a word starts (a letter right after a gap)
fn isgap c uchar to bool
if eq c 32
ret true
end
if eq c 10
ret true
end
ret eq c 9
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 2
end
n = ulong r
c = ulong 0
prev = true
for i ulong n
g = isgap get inb i
if not g
if prev
c = add c 1
end
end
prev = g
end
emitu c
say 0
ret 0
end

common_mistake: Checking 'did it run without errors?' instead of 'did it give the right answer?'. Both word counters exit 0. Fix: write expected answers for tricky inputs, compare exactly, and keep a known-wrong case to prove the check can say no.
evidence_note: The example compiled and ran on a Linux ARM64 computer (no GPU) and its output is recorded byte for byte, including a negative control. Rests on the recorded run: wc1 mismatched 3 of 4 inputs, wc2 matched 4 of 4, and the exit-0-only check passed both. NOT done: this is a teaching example, not a test suite for any product.
